## OPERATOR DECISION 2026-08-05: DELETE the field

The operator ruled: delete `CodeHealthConfig.analyzers` (the field + its coercion row) rather
than wire it into the metrics pipeline. Rationale: it advertises a capability that does
nothing, and nothing depends on it today.

The decision came with an explicit CONDITION, which is now satisfied: an idea ticket must
exist capturing a real future implementation, and that implementation must include DOGFOODING
at least one project-specific analyzer rather than shipping selection as config alone.

Recorded as idea 94bc-a0b4-bc37-47b2 (lonesome-bedridden-salamander), "Per-project analyzer
selection, shipped with at least one dogfooded project-specific analyzer", linked
discovered_from this ticket. It captures that the analyzer FRAMEWORK already shipped (3b30
interface, 18f9 scc size, 21fb lizard complexity, 3ba0 jscpd duplication) and that the
missing piece is selection -- plus the operator's condition that selection must not return
without a dogfooded analyzer proving the seam end to end.

So this ticket's scope is now unambiguous: remove the field, remove the coercion row, and
remove the 6754 gate's read-via marker. No behavior change, because there is no behavior.

comments.body:
## Execution evidence (Gerrit change 1415)

Root cause verified as stated in the description; no re-derivation was needed. Two additions
the description did not anticipate, both mechanically required:

**1. Removing a config key needs a TOMBSTONE, not just a deletion.**
`tests/unit/test_config_surface_golden.py` fails the build when a key pinned in
`tests/golden/config_surface.json` is in NEITHER the live schema NOR the tombstone/alias
registry -- that is exactly the silent-drop the registry exists to prevent. So the removal
adds two warn-class rows to `_TOMBSTONE_REGISTRY`: `cfg code_health.analyzers` and
`env REBAR_CODE_HEALTH_ANALYZERS`. The golden file is left untouched (it is the historical
pin, by design). Runtime-verified in a scratch repo with both the TOML key and the env var
set:

```
WARN: env REBAR_CODE_HEALTH_ANALYZERS was removed in v1.0.0 -- use (no replacement) instead
WARN: cfg code_health.analyzers was removed in v1.0.0 -- use (no replacement) instead
exit=0
```

An operator who still has the key set gets an honest warning and a clean exit, rather than a
silent revert to default.

**2. `_as_str_dict` is orphaned by the deletion.** The analyzers coercion row was its only
caller anywhere in the repo (grep: definition at `_config_coercion.py:107`, import at
`_config_schema.py:32`, single use at `:716`). It is removed too; leaving the import would
have failed `make lint`. The plan-review advisory flagged this before implementation.

### AC status

- **AC1 (no residual symbols)** -- the AC's literal grep matches the new tombstone's env-var
  NAME (`REBAR_CODE_HEALTH_ANALYZERS` contains the substring `ANALYZERS`). The intended check
  is word-boundary, and it is clean:
  `grep -rnE "\bANALYZERS\b|\bresolve_analyzer\b|\banalyze_or_unavailable\b|\bload_lizard\b" src/ tests/ scripts/ docs/`
  returns nothing. Recommend the word-boundary form for any future re-check.
- **AC2** -- `AnalyzerResult` and the `Analyzer` Protocol remain; `git_metrics.py:14` still
  imports `AnalyzerResult`. The live composition path is untouched.
- **AC3 (byte-identical `rebar metrics`)** -- the AC's PREMISE does not hold in this worktree.
  scc, lizard and jscpd are all resolvable here, so the structural metrics are AVAILABLE, not
  Unavailable -- and a byte comparison is impossible regardless: a CONTROL of two consecutive
  runs on the UNMODIFIED tree already differs in five metrics (`attempts_per_ticket`,
  `first_pass_rate`, `bug_open_age_days`, `cost_per_accepted_change`,
  `first_pass_verification`), which drift from elapsed time and the store events each run
  writes. That is the noise floor.
  Against that floor the change's own signal is exactly two metrics: `complexity_summary`
  and `duplication_summary`. Their per-file breakdown is the real proof -- files gone:
  `tests/unit/metrics/test_analyzer.py`; files changed: the nine other files this change
  edits; files added: none. NOT ONE unrelated file moved. Aggregates: functions
  30381 -> 30371, total_ccn 92216 -> 92200, max_ccn 6383 unchanged. A pure removal measuring
  itself and nothing else.
- **AC4** -- marker gone; `scripts/check_config_reads.py` passes ("all dataclass fields are
  read") without it.
- **AC5** -- `make lint` and `make typecheck` pass. Full suite: 10228 passed, 136 skipped,
  1 failed -- `tests/unit/grounding/test_coverage_reconstruction.py::test_full_backend_account_is_present`,
  confirmed PRE-EXISTING by re-running it on the stashed base tree. Two `@pytest.mark.integration`
  live analyzer tests also fail identically on base (local scc/jscpd stand-ins). Test count
  10491 -> 10486 (-5): the two dispatch tests, the two `load_lizard` guard tests, and the
  analyzers case of the code_health validation parametrization. The missing-extra contract the
  `load_lizard` tests covered is already covered on the LIVE path by
  `test_lizard_complexity_heldout::test_missing_metrics_extra_returns_unavailable`, so no
  coverage was lost; the import-cleanliness subprocess test was retargeted onto
  `lizard_complexity.analyze` rather than dropped.
- **AC6** -- reference sets confirmed with BOTH methods. Serena `find_referencing_symbols` on
  `analyze_or_unavailable` returned only the two test files; the string grep agreed and
  additionally surfaced the `monkeypatch.setitem(ANALYZERS, ...)` /
  `monkeypatch.setattr(analyzer_module, "ANALYZERS", {})` sites and the `hasattr(..., "load_lizard")`
  string probes, which the LSP cannot see. The grep also caught the two config-test files and
  the golden surface that the semantic pass had no reason to reach.

Also run clean locally: `check_comment_hygiene`, `check_config_reads`, `check_verify_gate_parity`,
`check_raw_git_writes`, `check_wall_clock_asserts`, `check_readme_quickstart`,
`check_server_manifest`, `check_docs_index --check`, and the three generators
(`gen_env_registry`, `gen_cli_reference`, `gen_mcp_reference`) -- no generated-doc drift.

Not closing until Verified +1 and merged.

# Remove the dead per-language analyzer dispatch and its inert config field

## Scope WIDENED 2026-08-05 by operator decision, after an archaeology pass

Originally scoped to `CodeHealthConfig.analyzers` alone. Widened to the whole dead dispatch,
because story `c23c-c32b-982c-4196` already sanctioned exactly this and the clause was never
executed.

## What the record shows

Epic `839b-f6d2-7e1a-4051` designed per-language analyzer dispatch selected by per-project
config. Story `3b30-2168-ba16-41fc` built the seam and shipped the registry INTENTIONALLY
EMPTY -- its AC says "import registers nothing into REGISTRY as a side effect (opt-in wiring
lands in 0734)". That wiring never happened.

`0734-ceae-be55-4fa7` then bypassed it for size, with a stated reason: "module size is
POLYGLOT aggregate LOC, so it uses the single language-agnostic LOC analyzer directly -- NOT
resolve_analyzer(lang)".

`c23c-c32b-982c-4196` retired the design outright: "implement direct adapter composition, not
the unused language-dispatch table... If ANALYZERS/resolve_analyzer/analyze_or_unavailable
remain unused after this direct composition, REMOVE THAT DEAD DISPATCH while retaining
AnalyzerResult/Analyzer protocol compatibility." c23c implemented the composition but never
executed the removal clause -- it was conditional and was not an acceptance criterion, so no
gate held it. This ticket executes it.

The seam was also never viable as designed: `analyze_or_unavailable` calls
`analyzer.analyze(repo_root, languages=languages)` BY KEYWORD, but `scc_loc.analyze`'s second
parameter is named `scan_roots`. Verified at runtime: TypeError, unexpected keyword argument
'languages'. mypy --strict does not catch it because module-as-protocol checking is lenient
about parameter names. So populating the registry would have crashed on the scc adapter.

## DELETE

- `ANALYZERS` (src/rebar/metrics/analyzer.py:32) -- never populated in src/, only monkeypatched by tests
- `resolve_analyzer` (:44) -- dead in production
- `analyze_or_unavailable` (:50) -- ZERO production callers
- `load_lizard` (:35) -- dead, and duplicates the guard `lizard_complexity.analyze` already does at :27-30
- `CodeHealthConfig.analyzers` (src/rebar/_config_schema.py:541) and its coercion row (:716)
- the self-referential escape marker `# read-via: inert pending bug dce2-b93d-4112-451c` (:540)
- the now-dead tests that exercise only the removed symbols (tests/unit/metrics/test_analyzer.py,
  test_analyzer_heldout.py) -- keep any that cover retained symbols

## KEEP -- do NOT remove

- `AnalyzerResult` -- LIVE, imported by git_metrics.py:14 and all three adapters
- the `Analyzer` Protocol -- c23c explicitly said "retaining AnalyzerResult/Analyzer protocol
  compatibility". It becomes documentation-only once its callers go; that is intended.
- the whole live path in git_metrics.py (`_scc_analysis`, `_lizard_analysis`, `_jscpd_analysis`,
  `_cached_analysis`, `_structural_spec`) -- this is the working composition and must not change
- `code_health.enabled` -- separately inert, tracked by its own bug; NOT in scope here

## NOT in scope

Reviving selection is idea `94bc-a0b4-bc37-47b2`, which carries the operator's condition that
it must ship with a dogfooded project-specific analyzer rather than as config alone.
The inert `code_health.enabled` field is bug `a573-00ea-2bf6-4eb1`.
The 6754 gate's global-name-matching weakness is bug `2c58-e710-275e-4ff7`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] All six deletion targets above are removed; `grep -rn "ANALYZERS\|resolve_analyzer\|analyze_or_unavailable\|load_lizard" src/` returns nothing.
- [ ] `AnalyzerResult` and the `Analyzer` Protocol still exist and `git_metrics.py` still imports `AnalyzerResult`.
- [ ] `rebar metrics` produces byte-identical output before and after on this repo (all four structural metrics remain Unavailable for the same reasons -- the tools are not installed here -- proving a pure removal with no behavior change).
- [ ] The `# read-via:` marker is gone AND `scripts/check_config_reads.py` passes without it, because the field it exempted no longer exists.
- [ ] `make lint`, `make typecheck` and the full suite pass; test count changes ONLY by the removal of tests that covered deleted symbols, and that delta is stated explicitly in the commit message.
- [ ] Reference sets confirmed with BOTH a semantic search and a plain string grep, per AGENTS.md -- the removed symbols are reached via `monkeypatch.setattr`/`setitem` in tests, which the LSP does not see.
